lenses.sp: Wants a large, steady, cheap company with a strong balance sheet.
lenses.vd: In Benjamin Graham's spirit: a great business, but this lens's own price test fails.

ch.r: Market value above ₹5,000 crore
ch.w: Graham avoided small companies; ₹5,000 crore is our Indian translation of 'adequate size'.

ch.r: Current assets ÷ current liabilities ≥ 2
ch.w: For every ₹100 it owes within a year, it holds ₹222 of cash, stock and dues coming in.

ch.r: Long-term debt ≤ current assets − current liabilities
ch.v: Long-term debt ₹37 cr vs working capital ₹38,716 cr
ch.w: Graham wanted the short-term cushion alone to be able to repay long-term loans.

ch.n: A profit every year for 10 years
ch.r: Positive earnings in each of the last 10 years
ch.v: Profit in all 4 yrs we have
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see; the earlier years are not in the free data.

ch.r: Dividends every year for 20 years (India: 10 years)
ch.w: 39 dividends in 10 years with no gap longer than 18 months.

ch.n: Earnings per share up a third in 10 years
ch.r: EPS +33% over 10 years (3-year averages at each end)
ch.w: EPS (average of the first 2 vs last 2 years we have) moved +11%.

ch.r: PE ≤ 15 on 3-year average earnings
ch.w: You pay ₹23 for every ₹1 of average yearly profit over the last 3 yrs.
You pay ₹5.13 for every ₹1 of net worth.

ch.r: Price < √(22.5 × EPS × book value per share)
ch.w: With EPS ₹67.7 and book value ₹278 per share, Graham's ceiling price is ₹650.

lenses.st: Wonderful business at a fair price
lenses.sp: Wants a simple business with a lasting edge, high returns without debt, and trustworthy managers.
lenses.vd: In Warren Buffett's spirit: a great business, and the price passes both this lens's own price test and the fair-value check (₹1,424 vs fair value ₹1,646).

ch.r: Could you explain how it makes money in two sentences?
q: What does it sell, and to whom?
Will people still need this in 10 years?

ch.r: A lasting edge: brand, low cost, network or switching costs
q: Why can't a well-funded rival copy it?
Has it kept high returns through bad years?

ch.r: ROE ≥ 15% in at least 8 of the last 10 years, with debt-to-equity < 0.5
ch.w: Strong in 4 of the 4 yrs we can see.

ch.r: No loss in 10 years
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see.

ch.n: Doesn't eat its cash in capex
ch.r: Capex < 50% of operating cash flow (5-year sum)
ch.v: Capex was 6% of cash from operations over 4 yrs
ch.w: Of every ₹100 of cash the business brought in, ₹6 went back into plant and equipment.

ch.r: Share count up no more than 5% over the years we have
ch.w: Your slice of the company hasn't been shrunk by new share issues.

ch.r: Candid, sensible with capital, no governance red flags
ch.v: 0 red flags, 1 to check (checked: auditor changes, CFO/KMP changes, credit ratings, SEBI orders, promoter holding, pledge).
ch.w: Our automatic checks are a starting point only.
q: Do they admit mistakes in the annual report letter?
Have past acquisitions and capex paid off?

ch.n: Bought with a margin of safety
ch.r: Price ≥ 25% below estimated intrinsic value
ch.w: Needs the fair-value (DCF) estimate, which arrives in Stage 4.

lenses.st: Great business at a fair price; invert
lenses.sp: Prefers a great business at a fair price, and first asks how the investment could fail.
lenses.vd: In Charlie Munger's spirit: a great business, but this lens's own price test fails.

ch.r: Average ROCE ≥ 20% over 5 years
ch.w: For every ₹100 in the business it earned about ₹31 a year.

ch.r: PEG (PE ÷ EPS growth) below 2
ch.w: PE 21.0 against EPS growth of 3.8% a year.

ch.r: Promoters own ≥ 25% and have pledged none

ch.r: Debt-to-equity below 0.35

ch.r: EPS growth 20–25% a year

story.what_it_does: HCLTech is an IT services company that also sells software (HCLSoftware). In FY26 it earned ₹130,144 crore of revenue, with the top twenty clients making up 28.5% of it. It is putting more emphasis on AI work, with Advanced AI revenue at $219 million in Q2 FY27.
story.plans: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 2.5% to 4% in constant currency and an EBIT margin of 17.5% to 18.5%. It plans to grow AI-native services by 25% and to build an AI datacenter, with an initial ₹3,500 crore and 50 MW long-term. The board also commits to return at least 75% of net income to shareholders.
story.moat: The notes point to big, spread-out client relationships, with the top 5 clients at only 11.4% of revenue, and a large contracted backlog of ₹156,372 crore in remaining performance obligations. Attrition of 12.8% and ROIC of 39.4% (LTM to Dec-25) also suggest a steady operation. The notes do not describe a specific competitive edge beyond this.

scenarios.story: Strong deal bookings ($3.3 billion in Q2 FY27, up 27%) and a mega deal start to add revenue from Q1 of next year. Margin recovered to 18.2% and record net income came as restructuring costs eased.
signals_to_watch: Services mega deal revenue starting to contribute next year
New deal bookings staying near or above $3 billion a quarter

scenarios.story: Growth stays modest at about 2.6% in constant currency, inside the 2.5% to 4% guidance. Margins stay within the 17.5% to 18.5% band while AI revenue grows.
signals_to_watch: Constant-currency revenue growth against the 2.5% to 4% guidance

scenarios.story: AI-driven price deflation, cuts by two US telecom clients and a shrinking software business hold growth back. Management stayed cautious and would not raise the top end of guidance.
